children: U.S. stocks moved lower Friday after August employment figures came in well above forecasts, shifting attention toward the Federal Reserve's next policy decision.
The S&P 500 fell 0.16% to 7,735.23, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.33% to 53,509.63. The Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.04%.

The economy added 162,000 jobs last month, compared with economists' 56,000 estimate. The unemployment rate was 4.1%, matching expectations. The data increased market expectations for a rate increase at the Fed's Sept. 15-16 meeting, with futures pricing a 65% probability versus 55% before the release.

Investors may now focus on upcoming inflation figures for additional clues on monetary policy. Consumer and producer price reports due next week could influence expectations for the Fed's September decision.
What it means for stocks: Higher rate expectations may pressure growth shares, while defensive sectors could attract investors seeking shelter from policy uncertainty.

title: S&P 500, Dow Stumbles After 162,000 Jobs Send Fed Rate-Hike Odds Higher
